subject.title: [Security] Session hijacking vulnerability due to predictable sequence IDs in gateway client

question: Does the gateway security owner agree that event sequence prediction cannot cross the authenticated WebSocket connection boundary, or is private packet-level proof required before disposition?
rationale: Source and protocol evidence contradict the claimed exploit, but the protected security label reserves final trust-boundary disposition for a human security owner.

options.title: Close as non-exploitable
options.body: Confirm that per-socket event ordering and UUID request correlation are not credentials and close the report with the authenticated-dispatch evidence.

options.title: Request private protocol proof
options.body: Ask the reporter for exact frames, attacker prerequisites, network position, auth configuration, and a current-main demonstration that reaches another authenticated connection or session.

recommendation.title: Close as non-exploitable
recommendation.body: Confirm that per-socket event ordering and UUID request correlation are not credentials and close the report with the authenticated-dispatch evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: The history most strongly connects this person to the extracted gateway client, protocol documentation, and broader gateway connection implementation.
